assets.name: flight-v2
assets.prompt: Production 2D game animation atlas in smooth polished 3D illustration style, not pixel art. EXACTLY the same adult woman Tilin as the reference: long brown hair, rectangular black glasses, olive green crop t-shirt, loose blue jeans and beige sneakers. Fixed three-quarter side camera, same body proportions, same face, clothes and lighting for all frames. EXACTLY SIXTEEN separate full-body frames arranged in a precise FOUR COLUMNS by FOUR ROWS grid, chronological left to right top to bottom. Square canvas. Equal cells, each full silhouette contained within its cell, generous 6 percent transparent gutters, no overlaps, no clipped shoes or hair. Character physical scale remains identical in all cells; do not enlarge curled or lying poses. TRUE fully transparent alpha-zero background. No scenery, shadows, floor, motion trails, text, grid lines or props. Natural non-graphic arcade reaction, no injury or blood. Native orientation must face RIGHT throughout, like reference; do not turn her around. When horizontal her HEAD is toward LEFT and FEET toward RIGHT. Each adjacent frame should be a SMALL anatomical change, with flexible spine, counterbalancing arms, trailing hair, and gradual knee movement, no repeated drawings. Create a single fluid caught-and-thrown airborne animation. First pose exactly matches the reference's row2 column2: both knees lifted and bent closely to chest, hands near upper chest, torso still upright, suspended in air. Frames1-4 release from that tuck, chest recoils slightly back towardLEFT and both hands start opening. Frames5-8 continuously lean back further, spine flexes, thighs slowly extend, arms reach outward to balance. Frames9-12 lower the torso toward horizontal, knees still bent softly, hair and fingers follow the motion. Frames13-16 extend toward a cushioned sideways landing: the left-side head and shoulder lead, right-side feet follow, one forearm reaches down to brace. Final pose matches reference bottomright: nearly horizontal on side, supporting elbow just about to touch ground, head LEFT feet RIGHT. Keep the entire sequence close in camera scale to the original, with smooth drawing-to-drawing progression.
